recipes.title: Tuscan Lemon Chicken Piccata
recipes.description: Golden chicken cutlets in a bright lemon, garlic and caper sauce. Serve with roasted asparagus or a little angel hair pasta.
ingredients: {{4|boneless, skinless chicken breast|boneless, skinless chicken breasts}} (about {{1½ lb}})
¼ cup fresh parsley, chopped, plus more to garnish

steps.text: Pat {{4|chicken breast|chicken breasts}} dry and slice each in half horizontally to make {{8|thin cutlet|thin cutlets}}. Mix {{1 tsp}} salt, {{½ tsp}} black pepper and {{½ tsp}} Italian seasoning. Sprinkle over both sides.
Spread {{½ cup}} flour on a shallow plate. Coat each cutlet on both sides and shake off the excess. Discard the flour that touched the raw chicken.

Heat {{2 Tbsp}} olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat, dividing it over {{batches}}. Sear for 3–4 minutes per side, until each cutlet reaches 165°F at its thickest part. Transfer to a clean plate and tent loosely with foil.
Lower the heat to medium and melt {{2 Tbsp}} butter in the same skillet. Stir in {{3 cloves}} minced garlic and cook for about 30 seconds, just until fragrant.
Pour in {{¾ cup}} broth and {{1/3 cup}} lemon juice and scrape up the browned bits. Stir in {{2 Tbsp}} capers and zest from {{1 lemon}}. Simmer 3–4 minutes, until slightly reduced.
Return the chicken and any juices to the skillet and spoon the sauce over the top. Simmer for 2 minutes to warm through.
Scatter with {{¼ cup}} chopped parsley and a few extra lemon slices if you like. Serve with roasted asparagus, a green salad or angel hair pasta.

recipes.kitchenNote: Squeeze the lemons fresh and add a little extra zest at the very end. Leftover sauce is wonderful tossed through a bowl of buttered pasta the next day.

recipes.title: Blueberry Buttermilk Pancakes
recipes.description: Tall, tender buttermilk pancakes dotted with jammy blueberries. A slow Saturday morning on a plate.
ingredients: 3 Tbsp unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the pan

steps.text: Whisk {{2 cups}} flour, {{2 Tbsp}} sugar, {{2 tsp}} baking powder, {{1 tsp}} baking soda and {{½ tsp}} salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl whisk {{2 cups}} buttermilk, {{2 eggs}}, {{3 Tbsp}} melted butter and {{1 tsp}} vanilla. If you need a fraction of an egg, beat it separately before measuring.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and fold with a spatula until just combined. A few lumps are good. Let the batter rest for 5 minutes.
Warm a griddle or large skillet over medium heat. A drop of water should sizzle on contact. Wipe the pan dry, then brush it lightly with butter.

Plan on {{batches}}. Pour ¼ cup batter per pancake and divide {{1 cup}} blueberries across the tops. Cook 2–3 minutes, until bubbles pop and the edges set. Flip and cook 1–2 minutes more, until set in the center and golden underneath.
Keep finished pancakes in a 200°F oven while you cook the rest. Serve with a pat of butter and warm maple syrup.

recipes.kitchenNote: Don't press the pancakes after flipping. Let them rise on their own. Frozen blueberries work too; add them straight from the freezer so they don't bleed.

recipes.title: Provençal Ratatouille
recipes.description: Summer vegetables cooked one by one, then simmered together with tomato, thyme and good olive oil.
ingredients: 5 Tbsp olive oil, divided, plus more to finish
{{1|medium eggplant|medium eggplants}} (about {{1 lb}}), cut into ¾-inch cubes
{{2|medium zucchini|medium zucchini}}, cut into ¾-inch half-moons
{{1}} red and {{1|yellow bell pepper|yellow bell peppers}}, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 can (28 oz) whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand
1½ tsp salt, plus more to taste

steps.text: Heat {{2 Tbsp}} oil in a wide pot. Brown {{1 lb}} cubed eggplant over medium-high heat in {{batches}}, dividing the oil and {{¼ tsp}} salt among batches. Cook each for 8–10 minutes, stirring. Transfer to a bowl.
Cook {{2|sliced zucchini|sliced zucchini}} in {{batches}}, dividing {{1 Tbsp}} oil among batches. Cook each about 5 minutes, until lightly browned but still firm. Add to the eggplant.

Add {{2 Tbsp}} oil, {{1|diced onion|diced onions}}, {{1}} red and {{1|yellow bell pepper|yellow bell peppers}}. Cook 8–10 minutes over medium heat until soft, then stir in {{4 cloves}} sliced garlic for 1 minute.

Add {{1|28-oz can|28-oz cans}} of crushed whole tomatoes with juice, {{4 sprigs}} thyme, {{1|bay leaf|bay leaves}}, {{1¼ tsp}} salt and {{½ tsp}} pepper. Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, until slightly thickened.
Return the eggplant and zucchini to the pot, cover and simmer gently 15–20 minutes, until everything is tender but still holds its shape.
Remove the bay and thyme stems. Fold in {{¼ cup}} torn basil, taste for salt and finish with a thread of olive oil. Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.kitchenNote: Ratatouille is even better the next day, so make a big pot. Spoon leftovers over polenta or toast, or bake them with eggs cracked right on top.

recipes.title: Irish Soda Bread
recipes.description: A craggy, golden loaf made with just four ingredients and no yeast. From bowl to oven in ten minutes.
ingredients: 4 cups ({{500 g}}) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
1¾ cups ({{420 ml}}) cold buttermilk, plus a splash more if needed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and dust a baking sheet or cast-iron skillet with flour.
Whisk {{4 cups}} flour, {{1 tsp}} baking soda and {{1 tsp}} fine salt in a large bowl, then make a well in the center.
Measure {{1¾ cups}} cold buttermilk. Pour in most and stir until a soft, shaggy dough forms. Add the rest only if dry flour remains.
Turn the dough onto a floured counter and pat it into a round about 2 inches high. Divide a large batch into rounds of that same height. Handle it as little as possible to keep the loaf tender.
Set the round on the floured sheet or skillet. With a floured knife, score an X about ½ inch deep across the top, extending it nearly to the edges.

Bake on the middle rack. Start checking after {{smallBatch|20 minutes|35 minutes}}. The bread should be deep golden and sound hollow when tapped underneath. If it sounds dull, bake a few more minutes and check again.
Transfer to a wire rack and let the loaf cool before slicing. Wrap it loosely in a clean tea towel if you prefer a softer crust. Serve with salted butter.

recipes.kitchenNote: Granny always said the cross was there to let the fairies out. It's at its best the day it's baked, still a little warm, with plenty of good salted butter.

recipes.title: Grandma's Apple Crumble
recipes.description: Soft cinnamon apples under a buttery oat crumble, baked until bubbling. Pass the custard.

items: 2½ lb tart apples (about {{6}}), peeled, cored and sliced
½ cup ({{100 g}}) light brown sugar
½ cup ({{1 stick}}) cold unsalted butter, cubed
Custard, cream or vanilla ice cream, to serve
1 tsp unsalted butter, for greasing the dish

steps.text: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) with a rack in the middle. Rub {{1 tsp}} butter over the baking dish. Choose a dish that holds the filling in an even layer.
Peel and core {{2½ lb}} apples, then cut them into ¼-inch slices. Toss with {{¼ cup}} sugar, {{1 Tbsp}} lemon juice, {{1 Tbsp}} flour and {{1 tsp}} cinnamon. Spread evenly in the prepared dish.
Mix {{1¼ cups}} flour, {{½ cup}} brown sugar, {{½ cup}} oats, {{½ tsp}} cinnamon and {{¼ tsp}} salt. Rub in {{½ cup}} cold cubed butter with your fingertips until the mixture clumps like damp sand.
Scatter the crumble loosely over the apples, right to the edges. Don't press it down; the little gaps let it crisp.
Start checking after {{smallBatch|30 minutes|40 minutes}} of baking. The crumble is ready when the top is deep golden and the juices bubble thickly at the edges.
Let it settle for 10 minutes, then spoon into bowls with warm custard, cold cream or a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

recipes.kitchenNote: Use a mix of apples if you can, some sharp and some sweet. A handful of blackberries tucked in with the apples was always Grandma's late-summer secret.

recipes.title: Huevos Rancheros
recipes.description: Crisp-edged fried eggs on warm corn tortillas with black beans and a smoky ranchero sauce. A ranch-hand breakfast worth waking up for.

items: 2 Tbsp water, for warming the beans

steps.text: Heat {{1 Tbsp}} oil over medium heat. Cook {{½|chopped onion|chopped onions}} and {{1|minced jalapeño|minced jalapeños}} for 5 minutes, until soft. Add {{2 cloves}} garlic and {{½ tsp}} cumin and stir for 30 seconds.

Add {{1|14½-oz can|14½-oz cans}} diced tomatoes and {{½ tsp}} salt. Simmer for 10 minutes, until slightly thickened. Blend off the heat for a smooth sauce if desired. Stir in juice from {{½ lime}} and keep warm.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat. Brush {{8|tortilla|tortillas}} with about {{1 Tbsp}} oil. Plan on {{batches}}, frying about 30 seconds per side until soft and blistered. Wrap in a clean towel.
Put {{1|15-oz can|15-oz cans}} of drained beans in a saucepan with {{2 Tbsp}} water. Warm over medium-low heat, stirring, until steaming. Cover to keep warm.
Reduce the skillet to medium heat and add the remaining {{1 Tbsp}} oil. Divide {{8 eggs}} across {{batches}}. Cover and cook each batch until the whites and yolks are firm.
Put two tortillas and an even share of the warm beans on each plate. Top each serving with two eggs and spoon the warm ranchero sauce over and around them.
Divide {{1|sliced avocado|sliced avocados}} and {{½ cup}} queso fresco among the plates. Add cilantro and a lime wedge to each. Serve while the tortillas are warm.

recipes.kitchenNote: Make the sauce the night before; it only gets better. On busy mornings I crack the eggs straight into the simmering sauce, cover the pan, and call it breakfast.

recipes.title: Argentine Beef Empanadas
recipes.description: Flaky hand pies filled with cumin-spiced beef, sweet pepper, egg and olives, crimped by hand and baked until deep golden. Makes 12.

items: 3 cups ({{375 g}}) all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
½ cup ({{113 g}}) cold unsalted butter or lard, cubed
½ cup ({{120 ml}}) cold water, plus {{1–2 Tbsp}} as needed
{{1|red bell pepper|red bell peppers}}, finely diced
½ tsp crushed red pepper flakes
¼ cup pitted green olives, chopped

steps.text: Whisk {{3 cups}} flour and {{1 tsp}} salt. Rub in {{½ cup}} cold butter or lard. Beat {{1 egg}} before measuring if you need a fraction. Mix it in with {{½ cup}} water. Add a little more water if needed. Wrap and chill for 1 hour.
Heat {{1 Tbsp}} oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook {{1|diced onion|diced onions}} and {{1|diced red pepper|diced red peppers}} for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft.

Brown {{1 lb}} beef in {{batches}} over medium-high heat. Break it into crumbles and cook each batch for 6–8 minutes, until it reaches 160°F. Combine and stir in {{2 tsp}} paprika, {{2 tsp}} cumin, {{½ tsp}} pepper flakes and {{1 tsp}} salt.
Stir in {{4 scallions}}, spread the filling on a plate and chill for 30 minutes, until cold. Warm filling melts the dough and makes the empanadas leak.
Heat the oven to 400°F and line enough baking sheets with parchment. Roll the dough out thin, about 3 mm (1/8 inch), and cut {{12 rounds}} about 5 inches across, rerolling the scraps once.

Spoon 2–3 tablespoons filling onto each round. Divide {{2|chopped hard-boiled egg|chopped hard-boiled eggs}} and {{¼ cup}} olives among them, leaving a ½-inch border. Wet the rim, fold and seal with a fork.
Space the empanadas on the sheets and brush with {{1|beaten egg|beaten eggs}}. Plan on {{batches}} if baking one sheet at a time. Bake each sheet for 20–25 minutes, until deep golden brown.
Let the empanadas rest for 5 minutes on the baking sheet before serving. The filling will be very hot.

recipes.kitchenNote: The twisted rope edge is called the repulgue and takes a few tries; a fork crimp seals just as well. Unbaked empanadas freeze beautifully. Bake from frozen, adding 5 minutes.

recipes.title: Jamaican Rice and Peas
recipes.description: Fluffy rice simmered in coconut milk with red kidney beans, thyme, allspice and a whole Scotch bonnet for fragrance, not fire.
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz / 425 g) red kidney beans, drained and rinsed
Scotch bonnet pepper, to taste (up to 1 whole pepper)

steps.text: Rinse {{1½ cups}} rice in a sieve under cold water, swishing with your hand, until the water runs almost clear. Drain well.

In a lidded pot, combine {{1|13½-oz can|13½-oz cans}} coconut milk, {{1 cup}} water, {{1|15-oz can|15-oz cans}} drained beans, {{3 scallions}}, {{3 cloves}} garlic, {{4 sprigs}} thyme, {{6|allspice berry|allspice berries}} and {{1 tsp}} salt. Bring to a boil.
Stir in the rice, then nestle the whole Scotch bonnet on top. Leave a whole pepper unbroken for mild flavor. For a small batch, omit it or use a small piece for more heat. Return to a boil.
Cover tightly and reduce to the lowest heat that keeps a gentle simmer. Cook for 20–25 minutes without lifting the lid. Check at the end for tender grains and no liquid pooling at the bottom.
Take off the heat and rest, covered, for 10 minutes. Remove the whole pepper, scallions, thyme stems and any visible allspice berries. Fluff with a fork before serving.

recipes.kitchenNote: Sunday dinner always had rice and peas beside it. Lift that Scotch bonnet out carefully: if it bursts, the whole pot turns fiery. Dried beans soaked overnight taste best.

recipes.title: Crusty French Baguettes
recipes.description: Four simple ingredients, a few patient folds and a blast of steam make crackling crusts and open, chewy crumb. Makes 3.
ingredients: Rice flour or semolina, for dusting
Boiling water for steam (1 cup per oven batch)

steps.text: Stir {{4 cups}} bread flour and {{1½ cups}} lukewarm water until no dry flour remains. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Sprinkle {{1 tsp}} instant yeast and {{2 tsp}} fine sea salt over the dough. Squeeze them through with a wet hand for 3–4 minutes, until evenly mixed and smooth.
Cover the dough. Every 30 minutes for 2 hours, wet your hand and stretch each of the four sides up and over the center. Cover again after each of the four rounds of folds.
Tip onto a lightly floured counter, divide into portions using roughly two servings' worth of dough per loaf and roll each loosely into a short log. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.

Pat each log flat, fold the top third down and the bottom third up, then fold in half and seal the seam with the heel of your hand. Roll each portion into a log with tapered ends. Aim for about 14 inches for a standard loaf and less for a smaller portion.

Lay the loaves seam-side up in the folds of a floured towel, with folds separating them. Cover and proof for 45 minutes, until puffy. Meanwhile, heat the oven to 475°F with a baking steel and a sturdy metal pan on the rack below.

Turn the loaves seam-side down onto a peel dusted with rice flour or semolina. Use a bread lame or sharp knife to cut four shallow, overlapping slashes along each loaf. Slide the loaves onto the hot steel.

Plan on {{batches}}. For each batch, use oven mitts to carefully pour 1 cup boiling water into the hot metal pan from a long-spouted kettle. Keep your face clear of the steam and shut the oven. Start checking for a deep golden crust after {{smallBatch|16 minutes|22 minutes}}.
Cool on a rack for at least 30 minutes, listening for the crust crackle. Slicing too soon makes the crumb gummy.

recipes.kitchenNote: Don't fear a dark crust: that is where the flavour lives. Shaping takes practice, so don't worry if your first batch looks rustic; it still tastes like Paris.

recipes.title: Lemon Chicken and Rice
recipes.description: Golden chicken thighs, tender long-grain rice and a squeeze of lemon, all from the same skillet.
ingredients: {{4|boneless, skinless chicken thigh|boneless, skinless chicken thighs}} (about {{1¼ lb}})
1 cup long-grain white rice, rinsed and drained

steps.text: Zest {{1 lemon}} before squeezing. Keep the zest and juice separate. Rinse {{1 cup}} rice in a sieve under cold water, then drain thoroughly.

Pat {{4|chicken thigh|chicken thighs}} dry and season with {{¾ tsp}} salt and {{½ tsp}} pepper. Heat {{1 Tbsp}} oil in a deep skillet over medium-high heat. Brown in {{batches}} for 3–4 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Stir {{1|diced onion|diced onions}} in the drippings for 4 minutes. Add {{2 cloves}} minced garlic and the drained rice and stir for 1 minute.

Stir in {{1¾ cups}} broth and the zest. Scrape the skillet. Bring to a simmer, then add the thighs and juices. Cover and cook on low for 18–22 minutes. Use two pans if needed. Check for tender rice and 165°F in the thickest thigh.
Take the covered skillet off the heat for 5 minutes. Move the thighs to a clean plate, fluff the rice with a fork, and stir in the lemon juice and {{2 Tbsp}} chopped parsley.

recipes.kitchenNote: A tight-fitting lid helps the rice cook evenly. Keep it closed until the first check.

recipes.title: Creamy Chicken and Wild Rice
recipes.description: A cozy Minnesota-style soup with chicken, wild rice and vegetables in a light cream broth.
ingredients: ¾ cup whole wild rice, rinsed

steps.text: Melt {{1 Tbsp}} butter over medium heat. Add {{1|diced onion|diced onions}}, {{2|diced carrot|diced carrots}} and {{2|diced celery rib|diced celery ribs}}. Cook for 6 minutes, stirring occasionally, then add {{1 tsp}} thyme.
Stir in {{¾ cup}} wild rice and {{6 cups}} broth. Choose a pot with room to stir. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer partially covered for 30 minutes.
Lower {{1 lb}} chicken thighs into the soup. Cook for 15–20 minutes, until the thickest thigh reaches 165°F. Transfer the chicken to a clean board. Keep simmering if the rice is still firm.
Use two forks to pull the cooked thighs into bite-size pieces. Return the chicken and any juices to the pot before adding the cream.
Stir in {{¾ cup}} half-and-half and warm gently over low heat. Keep the soup below a boil and taste for salt and pepper before serving.

recipes.kitchenNote: Whole wild rice gives this soup its chewy texture. A wild rice blend will cook faster, so check the package.

recipes.title: Chicken Broccoli Rice Bake
recipes.description: Chicken, broccoli and cooked rice baked in a cheddar sauce with a crisp cracker topping.

steps.text: Set out {{3 cups}} cooked rice, {{2 cups}} shredded cooked chicken, {{1½ cups}} milk and {{½ cup}} chicken broth. Heat the oven to 375°F. {{smallBatch|Grease a baking dish that fits the filling in an even layer.|Grease two baking dishes to split the filling into even layers.}}

Microwave {{3 cups}} broccoli florets in {{batches}}, loosely covered, with a splash of water. Check each batch after {{smallBatch|1 minute|2 minutes}}. Drain once the broccoli is bright green and just tender.
Melt {{2 Tbsp}} butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in {{2 Tbsp}} flour and cook for 1 minute, whisking constantly.
Slowly whisk in {{1½ cups}} milk and {{½ cup}} chicken broth. Add {{½ tsp}} kosher salt and {{¼ tsp}} black pepper. Simmer for 3 minutes, then take off the heat and stir in {{1½ cups}} sharp cheddar.
Mix {{3 cups}} cooked rice, {{2 cups}} shredded cooked chicken and the drained broccoli with the sauce. Spread it in the prepared bakeware and sprinkle {{½ cup}} crushed crackers over the top.
Start checking after {{smallBatch|17 minutes|22 minutes}} of baking. The center should reach 165°F and the edges should bubble. Check each dish individually if you split the filling.
Remove the bake from the oven and let it stand for 5 minutes before scooping into portions.

recipes.kitchenNote: Rotisserie chicken and leftover rice make this a quick dinner.

recipes.title: Penne alla Vodka
recipes.description: Penne coated in a silky tomato and cream sauce with Parmesan and a little red pepper.
ingredients: ¼ tsp crushed red pepper flakes

steps.text: Boil {{12 oz}} penne in salted water. Start checking just before the package time so it stays a little firm. Scoop out {{1 cup}} pasta water before draining.

Heat {{2 Tbsp}} oil in a skillet over medium heat. Soften {{1 shallot}} for 3 minutes. Stir in {{2 cloves}} garlic, {{¼ tsp}} red pepper flakes and {{¼ cup}} tomato paste. Cook 3–4 minutes, until the paste darkens.
Measure {{¼ cup}} vodka. Take the skillet off the burner before pouring it in. Return to medium-low heat and simmer for 2 minutes. Stir in {{¾ cup}} cream and {{¼ cup}} reserved pasta water.
Add the penne and simmer for 1 minute, tossing to coat. Remove from the heat and stir in {{½ cup}} Parmesan. Add pasta water a splash at a time to loosen the sauce, and salt to taste.

recipes.kitchenNote: Cook the tomato paste until it turns brick red. That extra time gives the sauce a deeper flavor.

recipes.title: Parmesan Mushroom Risotto
recipes.description: Creamy Arborio rice with browned mushrooms, Parmesan and a spoonful of butter.

items: {{1|small yellow onion|small yellow onions}}, finely diced

steps.text: Bring {{5 cups}} broth to a gentle simmer in a saucepan, then keep it warm over low heat.

Heat {{1 Tbsp}} oil over medium-high heat. Cook {{12 oz}} mushrooms in {{batches}} in a single layer, dividing the oil if needed. Cook each batch for 7–9 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned. Season with {{¼ tsp}} salt and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium and melt {{1 Tbsp}} butter in the pan. Cook {{1|diced onion|diced onions}} for 4 minutes, stirring, until soft.

steps.lead: Toast the rice and add wine.
steps.text: Stir in {{1½ cups}} Arborio rice and cook for 1 minute. Pour in {{½ cup}} white wine and stir until most of it is absorbed.

Add warm broth about ½ cup at a time. Stir often and wait until most of each addition is absorbed before adding more. After 18–22 minutes, the rice should be creamy with a slight bite. Use only as much broth as needed.
Fold in the mushrooms, the remaining {{1 Tbsp}} butter and {{¾ cup}} Parmesan. Add a splash of warm broth if needed and season with pepper. Serve right away.

recipes.kitchenNote: The risotto should settle into the bowl when you spoon it in. Keep a little warm broth handy for the last stir.

recipes.title: Garlic Butter Baked Salmon
recipes.description: Salmon baked with lemon, garlic butter and parsley. Good with rice or roast potatoes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a sheet pan with parchment. Measure {{1 lemon}} and zest half of that amount. Cut one thin slice per fillet and save the rest for squeezing. Use two pans if needed.

Pat {{4 salmon fillets}} dry and arrange skin-side down. Mix {{3 Tbsp}} melted butter, {{3 cloves}} minced garlic, the lemon zest, {{¾ tsp}} salt and {{¼ tsp}} pepper. Brush over the fish and top each piece with a lemon slice.
Bake for 12–15 minutes. Check from the side with a thermometer and take each fillet out when its thickest part reaches 145°F. Finish with the reserved lemon juice and {{2 Tbsp}} parsley.

recipes.kitchenNote: Start checking thin tail pieces early. Pieces of similar thickness will finish together.

recipes.title: Baked Cod with Tomatoes
recipes.description: Flaky cod baked over blistered cherry tomatoes, briny olives and garlic.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss {{2 cups}} tomatoes, {{½ cup}} olives, {{3 cloves}} sliced garlic and {{½ tsp}} oregano with {{1 Tbsp}} oil in a baking dish. Roast for 12 minutes, until the tomatoes start to collapse.

Check {{4 cod fillets}} for pin bones and remove any. Pat dry and rub with {{1 Tbsp}} oil, {{½ tsp}} salt and {{¼ tsp}} pepper. Set the fillets between the tomatoes in one layer. Split between dishes if crowded.
Bake for 10–14 minutes, until a thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the cod reads 145°F.
Spoon the tomatoes and pan juices over the cod. Measure {{1 lemon}}, then squeeze half of that amount over the dish. Scatter {{2 Tbsp}} torn basil. Cut any remaining lemon into wedges.

recipes.kitchenNote: Serve with bread or a scoop of rice to catch the tomato juices.

recipes.title: Pan-Seared Trout Almondine
recipes.description: Crisp-skinned trout with toasted almonds, browned butter and lemon.
ingredients: {{4|skin-on trout fillet|skin-on trout fillets}} (4–6 oz each)

steps.text: Check {{4|trout fillet|trout fillets}} for pin bones and pull out any with tweezers. Pat both sides dry and sprinkle the fillets evenly with {{½ tsp}} salt and {{¼ tsp}} pepper.

Heat {{1 Tbsp}} oil in a skillet over medium-high heat, dividing it among {{batches}}. Sear skin-side down for 3–4 minutes per batch. Press lightly if the skin curls. Finish the other side before starting the next batch.
Flip the fillets in the skillet and cook for 1–2 minutes per batch, until the thickest part reaches 145°F. Transfer to warm plates, skin-side up, and repeat both sides with any remaining fillets.
Lower the heat to medium. Stir {{3 Tbsp}} butter and {{1/3 cup}} almonds for 2–3 minutes, until golden and nutty. Take off the heat and stir in {{1 Tbsp}} lemon juice and {{2 Tbsp}} parsley.
Spoon the almond butter around the fillets and serve immediately. Keep the trout skin-side up so it stays crisp.

recipes.kitchenNote: Keep the fillets skin-side up after cooking so the skin stays crisp.

recipes.title: Strawberry Lemonade
recipes.description: Pink lemonade with blended strawberries and fresh lemon juice. Eight servings fill a two-quart pitcher.
ingredients: 3½ cups cold water, plus more to make {{8 cups}}
Ice and lemon slices, for serving

steps.text: Rinse the strawberries under cold water. Drain, remove the leafy tops, and halve the berries. Measure {{3 cups}} of the halved berries.
Whisk {{¾ cup}} sugar into {{1 cup}} warm water until you can no longer see sugar crystals. Let the mixture cool slightly before blending.
Add the strawberries and sugar water to a blender. Blend for 30–45 seconds, until no large pieces remain. Split the mixture into batches if it exceeds the blender's fill line.
Set a fine-mesh strainer over a pitcher large enough for the batch. Pour in the berry mixture and press it through with the back of a spoon. Discard the seeds left in the strainer.
Roll the lemons on the counter, halve them and squeeze. Strain out the seeds and measure exactly {{1 cup}} of juice. Stir it into the strawberry mixture along with {{3½ cups}} of cold water.
Add more cold water a little at a time until the lemonade measures {{8 cups}}. Stir well and chill. Pour over ice in {{8 glasses}} and add a lemon slice to each.

recipes.kitchenNote: If the pitcher has no markings, first measure in the total volume of water specified in the final step and mark the level. Empty it before mixing.

recipes.title: Midwest Lemonade Shake-Up
recipes.description: State fair-style lemonade shaken with squeezed lemon wedges and ice. Eight servings fill a two-quart pitcher.
ingredients: {{8|squeezed lemon wedge|squeezed lemon wedges}}, saved from juicing
5 cups cold water, plus more to make {{8 cups}}
2 cups ice for shaking, plus extra ice for serving

steps.text: Scrub the lemons before cutting them into quarters. Squeeze {{1½ cups}} juice through a strainer into a large bowl. Set aside {{8|squeezed wedge|squeezed wedges}} and discard the seeds.
Whisk {{1 cup}} sugar into {{1 cup}} cold water until dissolved. Add to the lemon juice, then stir in the remaining {{4 cups}} measured water.
Divide the lemonade base, squeezed wedges and {{2 cups}} ice into {{batches}}. Load one batch into a quart jar with a tight lid. Keep it below two-thirds full so the ice can move.
Shake each batch for 20 seconds. Strain it into a pitcher large enough for the batch, then empty the jar. Repeat until all of the lemonade base, wedges and ice have been used.
Discard the strained ice and wedges. Add cold water to bring the pitcher to {{8 cups}} and stir. Divide the lemonade among {{8 glasses}} filled with fresh ice.

recipes.kitchenNote: Use a quart jar and leave room for the ice to move. Shaking the squeezed wedges releases lemon oil from the peel.

recipes.title: Bitters-Heavy Lemonade
recipes.description: Tart lemonade with aromatic bitters and lemon peel. Eight servings fill a two-quart pitcher.
ingredients: 48–64 dashes aromatic bitters, alcohol-free if desired
8 strips lemon peel and ice, for serving

steps.text: If making syrup, stir {{½ cup}} sugar into {{½ cup}} hot water until dissolved. Let it cool and measure {{¾ cup}}. If using prepared syrup, measure {{¾ cup}} straight from the bottle.

Strain the seeds from the lemon juice. Measure {{1¼ cups}} of juice and {{¾ cup}} of simple syrup into a pitcher large enough for the batch. Stir in {{48 dashes}} of aromatic bitters, which gives about 6 dashes per serving.
Stir in {{5½ cups}} cold still water. Taste a small sip. For a stronger flavor, add bitters a dash at a time, up to {{64 dashes}} total.
Top up with cold water until the pitcher holds {{8 cups}}. Stir, then divide among {{8|ice-filled glass|ice-filled glasses}}. Twist a strip of lemon peel over each glass and drop it in.

recipes.kitchenNote: Use chilled still water and ice. Bitters vary in strength, so taste after the first addition before adding more.

recipes.title: Vanilla Cream Cheese Cupcakes
recipes.description: Vanilla cupcakes made with Pillsbury white cake mix and topped with Pillsbury cream cheese frosting.
ingredients: ½ box Pillsbury Moist Supreme White Cake Mix
{{½}} of the box amounts for water, vegetable oil and eggs
1 tub (16 oz) Pillsbury Creamy Supreme Cream Cheese Frosting

steps.text: Set a rack in the middle of the oven. Heat the oven to the cupcake temperature on the cake mix box. Put paper liners in {{12 standard muffin cups}}.

Weigh out {{½}} of the dry mix. Measure {{½}} of the water, oil and eggs listed on the box. Beat the eggs before measuring a fraction of them. Mix these with the dry mix and {{1 teaspoon}} vanilla for the time shown on the box.
Divide the batter evenly among the paper liners. Fill each cup about two-thirds full so the tops have room to rise.
Bake on the middle rack for the cupcake time on the cake mix box. Start checking at the low end of the range. The cupcakes are ready when a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Let the cupcakes sit in the pans for 5 minutes. Lift them out carefully and transfer them to a wire rack.
Cool on the rack for about 30 minutes, or until the sides and tops feel cool.
Set out {{1|16-oz tub|16-oz tubs}} of frosting and stir until smooth. Spread about 1½ tablespoons on each fully cooled cupcake or pipe a swirl. Add sprinkles if you like.

recipes.kitchenNote: For fractional eggs or egg whites, whisk them first and measure the indicated portion by weight or volume. Check the box for ingredient amounts.

recipes.title: Steak-Seasoned Skillet Pork Chops
recipes.description: Worcestershire-marinated pork chops with steak seasoning, mashed potatoes and garlic green beans.

items: 1 tsp kosher salt, for the potato water
¼ cup milk, plus more as needed
{{4|boneless pork loin chop|boneless pork loin chops}}, about 1 inch thick
1 Tbsp neutral cooking oil, for the skillet

steps.text: Pat {{4|pork chop|pork chops}} dry. Stir {{2 tablespoons}} Worcestershire sauce, {{2 teaspoons}} steak seasoning and {{½ teaspoon}} garlic powder in a shallow dish. Turn each chop in the mixture to coat both sides.
Cover and refrigerate for 15–30 minutes. Start the potatoes while the chops marinate.
Cut {{1½ lb}} potatoes into 1-inch chunks. Cover with cold water by 1 inch and add {{1 tsp}} salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 14–17 minutes, until fork-tender.
Drain the potatoes and return them to the warm pot. Mash in {{2 tablespoons}} butter and {{¼ cup}} milk. If needed, add milk 1 tablespoon at a time. Cover to keep warm.

Lift the chops from the marinade, blot dry and discard the marinade. Plan on {{batches}}. Divide {{1 tablespoon}} oil among batches. Heat the skillet over medium-high heat. Sear for 3–4 minutes per batch, then cook the other side before starting the next.

Flip the chops in the skillet and reduce to medium. Cook each batch for 3–5 minutes more, until a thermometer inserted from the side reads 145°F at the thickest part. Transfer to a clean plate and repeat both sides with any remaining chops.
Rest each batch on a clean plate for at least 3 minutes before serving. When the last chops leave the skillet, cook the green beans in the same pan.
Add {{12 oz}} green beans and {{¼ cup}} water to the same skillet over medium heat. Cover and cook for 4–5 minutes, until crisp-tender. Uncover and let any remaining water cook off.
Stir {{1 tablespoon}} butter and {{2 cloves}} minced garlic into the beans. Cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant. Serve with the pork chops and mashed potatoes.

recipes.kitchenNote: Steak seasoning blends vary in saltiness. Taste the beans and potatoes before adding extra salt, and use a clean plate for the cooked chops.

recipes.title: Italian Beef Rigatoni Skillet
recipes.description: Rigatoni with browned ground beef, garlic and crushed tomatoes, finished with Parmesan.
ingredients: ½ tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
½ cup grated Parmesan, plus more for serving

steps.text: Set a large pot of salted water over high heat. Dice {{1|onion|onions}} and mince {{3 cloves}} garlic. Wait to add the pasta until the sauce is simmering.
Heat {{1 Tbsp}} oil in a deep skillet over medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook for 4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened.
Brown {{1 lb}} beef in {{batches}}. Break each batch into crumbles and cook for 6–8 minutes, until it reaches 160°F. Combine the browned beef and spoon off excess grease.
Stir the garlic, {{1 tsp}} Italian seasoning and {{½ tsp}} salt into the beef for 30 seconds. Stir in {{1|28-oz can|28-oz cans}} crushed tomatoes and simmer uncovered for 8–10 minutes.
While the sauce simmers, add {{12 oz}} rigatoni to the boiling water. Cook until al dente using the package timing. Scoop out {{½ cup}} pasta water, then drain.

Combine the rigatoni and sauce in the skillet or pasta pot. Toss over low heat for 1 minute, adding pasta water 1 tablespoon at a time if needed. Turn off the heat, stir in {{½ cup}} Parmesan and finish with {{2 Tbsp}} basil if using.

recipes.kitchenNote: Save the pasta water before draining. A splash helps the sauce coat the tubes of rigatoni.
